players.product: ESC AI servers and GB200 / GB300 NVL72 racks

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Nick Wu: Q2 2026 set all-time highs for brand consolidated revenue, operating profit and net profit after tax. Revenue TWD 241 billion (+39% YoY), operating profit TWD 19.6 billion (+230% YoY), net profit after tax TWD 19 billion (+94% YoY), EPS TWD 25.6; growth was driven mainly by AI servers and PCs. Co-CEO S.Y. Hsu: the first quarter in which brand revenue passed TWD 200 billion; server revenue doubled in Q2. Revenue mix: System Business Group 45%, Open Platform Business Group 19%, Infrastructure Solutions Business Group 36%; by region Asia Pacific 50%, Europe 35%, Americas 15%.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue TWD 241 billion (+39% YoY); operating profit TWD 19.6 billion (+230%); net profit TWD 19 billion (+94%); EPS TWD 25.6; ISBG 36% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 outlook (CFO): quarter-on-quarter growth of 15%-20% for PCs, 5%-10% for components and 10%-15% for servers; year on year PC growth is expected to exceed 20% and servers over 150%. Co-CEO Samson Hu: the 2026 server growth target is revised from the 100% given at the last quarterly conference to at least 150% YoY; specific 2027 server targets will be clearer by Q4. Management: the Q3 PC growth splits roughly 50/50 between ASP and shipment volume, each rising 5% to 10%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 QoQ: PC 15%-20%, components 5%-10%, servers 10%-15%; servers over 150% YoY; 2026 server target at least 150% (was 100%)

quarterly_data.signal: Co-CEO Samson Hu on the AI server mix: HGX-type servers were approximately 60% and NVL72 GB300 full rack systems approximately 30% of Q2 server revenue (first half overall roughly 65% to 35%); together about 90% of server revenue, the remaining 10% general purpose servers and miscellaneous products. He expects the customer base to be more diversified next year and says server profitability has reached a very healthy industry level. CFO: with the ramp-up of new products like the GB300 and economies of scale, server segment profitability has increased.
quarterly_data.figure: HGX approximately 60%, GB300 NVL72 racks approximately 30% of Q2 server revenue; about 90% combined

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Nick Wu: server orders and order book show incredibly strong momentum, and ASUS's current operational and financial resources are reaching a point where they cannot fully satisfy all the orders received, so the company plans to increase investment in operational resources and financial preparations, also for the AI PC and HPC upgrade cycles expected over the next 2 to 3 years. Co-CEO S.Y. Hsu: given current order visibility, ASUS expects a prolonged period of AI server growth this year.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (orders exceed current operational and financial resources)

quarterly_data.signal: Co-CEO Samson Hu on server components: memory supply remains tight with allocation priority skewed clearly towards server demand; server memory is in a better position than PC memory, and CPU vendors likewise give servers higher allocation priority than PCs. Supply is not 100% sufficient, but the shortage is within ASUS's controllable range and has not caused significant operational disruption. CFO: Q2 inventory rose significantly to TWD 339.9 billion, largely from strategic stockpiling of high unit price and critical components to support Q3 and second-half demand.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory TWD 339.9 billion (strategic stockpiling of critical components)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Nick Wu: Q2 gross and operating margins reached historical highs on brand position, product mix and supply chain resilience. He expects the whole PC market's ASP to grow by over 20% due to rising memory prices, with ASUS capturing a larger value premium. ASUS uses a 4%-5% operating margin as its baseline for reasonable profitability and expects Q3 profitability to likely remain above the upper end of that range; over the next 1-2 years server growth is expected to be substantially larger than the PC / motherboard / gaming side, which has a different margin profile.
quarterly_data.figure: operating margin baseline 4%-5%; Q3 expected above the upper end; market ASP over 20% growth (CFO view)

quarterly_data.signal: PCs: PC revenue grew 20% YoY in Q2 despite rising RAM component costs; high-value products (gaming, high-end Copilot+ PCs, non-Chromebook convertibles) are 65% of the product mix; commercial PC growth reached 58% YoY, above 50% for 6 consecutive quarters, helped by orders from several major banks in Southeast Asia. Co-CEO S.Y. Hsu: the mainstream forecast for 2026 global PC shipments is a decline of approximately 4%, and with H1 early stocking he predicts the second-half decline will exceed 10%; high-end products are less affected by memory costs.
quarterly_data.figure: PC revenue +20% YoY; commercial PC +58% YoY; high-value products 65% of mix; 2026 global PC shipments approximately -4%, H2 decline to exceed 10% (management view)

quarterly_data.signal: Open Platform Business Group (Co-CEO Samson Hu): Q2 revenue declined approximately 10%-15% YoY on key component cost headwinds, as memory price hikes hurt end demand for motherboards and graphics cards; ROG monitors grew 20% and accessories over 50% YoY, and NUC revenue rose 30% driven by the NVIDIA-branded Ascent GX10 (Q2 GX10 shipments 3 times those of its first quarter). He sees memory price increases slowing but still rising in the second half and believes boards and cards can gradually return to growth.
quarterly_data.figure: OPBG revenue down approximately 10%-15% YoY; NUC revenue +30%; GX10 shipments 3 times

quarterly_data.signal: NVIDIA RTX Spark products: ASUS is in the first wave of manufacturers launching RTX Spark systems; the ProArt P16 and P14 notebooks are expected to begin sales in Q4 2026, aligned with the key partner's schedule, and the initial planned quantities have been fully pre-ordered by channel partners, with additional orders being placed. A GR1X desktop on the RTX Spark platform is being prepared for Q4. The Zenbook 14 (from $799) is expected to launch in Q3.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (ProArt P16 / P14 sales start Q4 2026; initial quantities fully pre-ordered)

quarterly_data.signal: Co-CEO S.Y. Hsu on the ZenAi CLAU agentic AI integrated into ASUS laptops: the local model is a fine-tuned open source small language model of approximately 4 billion parameters that offloads complex queries to a cloud model; for commercial PCs ASUS integrated VRAM virtualization technology from an unnamed Taiwan-based flash controller vendor to run larger models and cut token costs.
